Cascading ice–rock avalanche multi-hazard early warning in the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli River Corridor | PreventionWeb

 Author(s) Bapon SHM Fakhruddin Dhiraj Pradhananga Kumar Aryal et.al 

# Cascading ice–rock avalanche multi-hazard early warning in the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli River Corridor 

Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute

This article examines the cascading ice-rock avalanche and flood event that occurred on 26 August 2026 in the Bhote Koshi-Trishuli corridor of the Nepal Himalaya. The study reconstructs the event chronology and downstream propagation by synthesizing seismic, terrain, hydrological, and documentary records. Apparent celerity was calculated for three river reaches spanning approximately 196 km, covering intervals from the Langtang Lirung source area to Devghat. Remote sensing, satellite imagery, and documentary observation were used to characterise geomorphic changes, while a deterministic sensitivity analysis assessed uncertainties related to timing, distance, and terrain. An assessment of early-warning system elements was conducted using documentary evidence and a 10-element framework.

The study found rapid downstream propagation with pronounced decreases in celerity, from 47.3 m/s in the uppermost reach to 6.0 m/s downstream, with the entire cascade unfolding within about 6 hours and 43 minutes. However, there was insufficient evidence to verify fully operational, end-to-end early warning capabilities along the corridor. The authors propose a two-stage warning framework: first, evidence-based hazard screening and operational readiness; second, scenario development and emergency escalation. They recommend linking hazard detection and operational functions, integrating various observational data, maintaining institutional and financial readiness, and ensuring direct emergency response even with incomplete monitoring. The framework provides a transparent basis for early warning in high-mountain, multi-hazard contexts with limited observational evidence.

# Cascading Ice–Rock Avalanche Multi-Hazard Early Warning in the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli River Corridor 

 October 28, 2026 

## Abstract

Cascading hazards in high-mountain environments can evolve rapidly from slope failure to destructive downstream flooding, challenging conventional early-warning systems. The 26 August 2026 Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche and subsequent flood cascade along the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli corridor were examined through a retrospective synthesis of seismic, terrain, hydrological and documentary evidence. Event chronology reconstruc-tion and reach-based analysis yielded apparent celerities of 47.3, 20.9 and 6.0 m s−1 across successive reaches of 22, 44 and 130 km. Propagation over the approximately 196 km cor-ridor occurred within 6 h 43 min of the catalogued seismic marker. Deterministic sensitiv-ity analysis preserved the downstream decline in celerity under the specified timing and distance perturbations, although uncertainty in event initiation, flow formation and ob-servational timing limits hydraulic interpretation. The warning-chain assessment identi-fied insufficient evidence to verify end-to-end operational capability. A two-stage frame-work is proposed, which combines evidence-based hazard screening, operational readi-ness, scenario development and direct emergency escalation.

# Early warning

An integrated system of hazard monitoring, forecasting and prediction, disaster risk assessment, communication and preparedness activities systems and processes that enables individuals, communities, governments, businesses and others to take timely action to reduce disaster risks in advance of hazardous events. Early warning systems are a key component of disaster risk management activities.

Early Warnings for All is a groundbreaking initiative to ensure that everyone on Earth is protected from hazardous weather, water, or climate events through life-saving early warning systems by the end of 2027. Stay informed about the groundbreaking "Early Warnings for All" initiative.

 

In Mozambique, experience from past disasters has helped shape a powerful national system for disaster risk reduction.
